data.turoyo: <...> ʕǦənne u margayḏan, dʕəkke u nafalawo w ʕəndakkawo, u mede, d kit, d səmme b qarʕe du margayḏan, b qarʕe d tə isane l aṯi. <...>
data.translation: <...> Sie haben unsere Wiese zertrampelt und all den Klee, all die duftenden Kräuter niedergetreten! Das, was sie mit unserer Wiese angestellt haben, das hat noch kein Mensch erlebt. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; plural l-agent assimilation and new meadow participant.

summary: All three records checked. Attributive ʕǧine gives the result state of pressed dates, not an additional eventive Detransitive clause.
The l-series ʕǦənne denotes trampling a meadow and supports ordinary stem-I stampfen with an extended patient.
The acknowledged mʕaǧno example at 30/13 is not promoted to a new stem. A single m-prefixed modifier cannot establish II versus III or exclude borrowing.
Existing Arabic etymology and the uncertainty note are retained verbatim in the human entry.
Ask a speaker/editor to resolve mʕaǧno at 30/13: productive II/III Part. Pass., lexicalized modifier or borrowed Arabic adjective? Obtain base forms before adding a stem.
Confirm whether kneading and stamping warrant a future gloss distinction; current evidence supports the inherited broad stampfen without renumbering.
Stamping a meadow extends the affected object from food to ground/vegetation; retain stampfen.
